frozen_note: Written from textbook macro-finance theory before corpus retrieval or LLM assessment; no asset-return data is used anywhere in this project. Signs are conditional THEORETICAL assumptions, not estimates.

nodes.label: Consumer spending strength (retail-sales surprise)
nodes.observable_at_cutoff: Census advance retail sales, July 2023: +0.7% m/m vs +0.4% consensus

edges.condition: Holds when higher nominal sales translate into revenue growth without offsetting margin compression (e.g. from input-cost or wage pressure, discounting, or mix shift).
edges.mechanism: Retail and food-service sales are revenue for consumer-facing firms; aggregate profits are pro-cyclical.
edges.retrieval_question: Is strong consumer spending or retail demand raising company sales, revenue, earnings, or guidance?
edges.retrieval_query: consumer spending demand sales revenue earnings guidance outlook comparable sales customers traffic net sales increased raised guidance

edges.condition: Holds holding discount rates constant (cash-flow news channel).
edges.mechanism: Present-value identity: higher expected cash flows raise prices for given discount rates.
edges.retrieval_question: Do companies report or expect higher earnings, profit growth, buybacks, or shareholder returns?
edges.retrieval_query: earnings per share net income operating income profit growth record results share repurchase dividend shareholders raised full-year outlook

edges.condition: Holds when the economy is near capacity / the labour market is tight, so excess demand shows up in prices rather than quantities.
edges.retrieval_question: Is strong demand or consumer spending adding to inflation pressure, prices, or wage growth?
edges.retrieval_query: demand inflation pressure prices rising consumer prices wage growth tight labor market services inflation core inflation elevated

edges.condition: Holds when inflation is above target and the central bank's reaction function is data-dependent.
edges.mechanism: Policy-rule (Taylor-rule) reaction to inflation; long rates react to macro news.
edges.retrieval_question: Does inflation or strong economic data imply further Federal Reserve rate increases or keeping rates higher?
edges.retrieval_query: inflation federal funds rate additional policy firming increase rates restrictive data dependent tighten hold rates steady

edges.condition: Holds when the rate increase is not offset by stronger expected cash flows; sign of the TOTAL effect of good macro news on equities is state-dependent.
edges.mechanism: Higher discount rates lower present values; good news can be bad for stocks in expansions.
edges.retrieval_question: Are higher interest rates or tighter financial conditions weighing on valuations, asset prices, credit, or demand?
edges.retrieval_query: higher interest rates tighter financial credit conditions borrowing costs asset prices valuations equity prices weigh on economic activity

ordinary_baseline.question: How did the July 2023 retail sales report affect the outlook for US equities?
ordinary_baseline.query: July 2023 retail sales consumer spending effect outlook equities stocks economy

theory_vs_evidence_note: References establish that each mechanism is theoretically/empirically plausible IN GENERAL. Whether a mechanism was ACTIVE around 2023-08-15 is judged only from the point-in-time corpus by the evidence assessor.
